<section id="research"><div class="section-head"><div><h1 class="page-heading">Research</h1></div></div><div class="research">
<article class="project"><span class="project-num">01 — SPATIAL GENOMICS</span><h3>Mapping glioblastoma from core to edge</h3><p>I led the analysis of a 22-sample Visium cohort with matched Xenium and single-nucleus RNA-seq to map tumor and immune states across anatomical niches. Niche-restricted interaction analysis reveals how cellular communication depends on tissue context.</p><div class="tags"><span class="tag">Visium · Xenium</span><span class="tag">BANKSY · RCTD · CellTrek</span><span class="tag">CellChat · NicheNet</span></div><a href="https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.04.04.647096" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read the preprint · Equal-contribution first author ↗</a></article>
<article class="project"><span class="project-num">02 — TUMOR IMMUNOLOGY</span><h3>Understanding checkpoint blockade response</h3><p>Using single-cell transcriptomes from syngeneic glioma models, I studied divergent responses to PD-1 blockade, linking response to progenitor versus terminally exhausted CD8+ T-cell states and the influence of CD4 T cells.</p><div class="tags"><span class="tag">scRNA-seq</span><span class="tag">T-cell exhaustion</span><span class="tag">Immunotherapy</span></div><a href="https://doi.org/10.1136/jitc-2022-005293" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read the paper · Equal-contribution first author ↗</a></article>
<article class="project"><span class="project-num">03 — SINGLE-CELL MULTI-OMICS</span><h3>Decoding tumor ecosystems and evolution</h3><p>I integrate genetic and transcriptional data to connect mutations with cellular programs, from meningioma and the vestibular schwannoma ecosystem to relapse-associated states in acute myeloid leukemia.</p><div class="tags"><span class="tag">scRNA-seq · WES · WGS</span><span class="tag">Tumor evolution</span><span class="tag">Microenvironment</span></div><a href="https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42762-w" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Explore the schwannoma atlas ↗</a></article>
<article class="project"><span class="project-num">04 — MACHINE LEARNING</span><h3>Learning the signals of RNA modification</h3><p>I developed MU-PseUDeep, a convolutional neural network that combines RNA sequence and predicted secondary structure to identify pseudouridine sites in human, mouse, and yeast.</p><div class="tags"><span class="tag">Deep learning</span><span class="tag">RNA structure</span><span class="tag">Epitranscriptomics</span></div><a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csbj.2020.07.010" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Read the method · First author ↗</a></article></div></section>
